title: Killing the Messenger: David's Policy or Politics?
author: Pamela Tamarkin Reis
publisher: Journal for the Study of the Old Testament 30.3 (SAGE)
allowedUseNotes: Copyrighted peer-reviewed journal article. Project stores its own summary of the argument only; no reproduction of article text.
summary: A literary-critical reading of David's pattern of executing messengers who bring him news of a rival's death (the Amalekite in 2 Samuel 1; the killers of Ish-bosheth in 2 Samuel 4), arguing the executions track David's political advantage rather than a consistent moral policy. Reis reads David as genuinely deceived by 'the lying Amalekite' in 2 Samuel 1 — taking the messenger's account of killing Saul at face value at the time — and argues David only learns the true circumstances of Saul's death later, by the time of 2 Samuel 4. This directly supports reading the Amalekite's account as a self-serving fabrication (this project's view-amalekite-fabrication), with a named, checkable, peer-reviewed source rather than only a hedged 'e.g., commentators' attribution.
